text.p: -- Unocal Corp shares will not be damaged by U.S. legislation implementing trade sanctions against new investment in Burma, Schroder Wertheim analyst Michael Mayer said in a research report.
-- The legislation will apply only to new projects, not the existing Unocal operations there.

-- "The Burma sanctions are a cloud over Unocal, but have been a negative valuation factor for months. We continue to believe that Unocal is the most attractive stock among the major oils and it remains on our recommended list," Mayer said.

-- Unocal has a 28.6 percent interest in the $1.2 billion offshore Yadana natural gas field and first production is expected in mid-1998 at 525 million cubic feet per day, rising to 650 mmcf per day by 1999.
-- Yadana will account for three percent of Unocal's forecast $2.55 earnings per share in 1998 and six percent of a forecast $2.95 in 1999.
-- By 1100 EDT/1500 GMT Unocal stock was trading up 1/4 at 37-5/8 and Mayer has a target price of 43.
